newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Surgut says share issue broke law -commission.
newsitem.headline: Surgut says share issue broke law -commission.

text.p: The head of Russia's NK Surgutneftegaz (Surgut Holding) oil company has acknowledged a recent share issue by its AO Surgutneftegaz production unit violated securities law, a Federal Commission for the Securities Market spokesman said on Tuesday.

Surgut Holding president Vladimir Bogdanov signed documents setting out measures to eliminate the legal violations on Tuesday after a meeting with securities commission chairman Dmitry Vasilyev, the spokesman said.

He said this would involve an extraordinary shareholders meeting to amend the company's charter. Holders of voting stock would be given the right to acquire new ordinary shares in AO Surgutneftegaz in proportion to their holdings.

"Yesterday Vasilyev met Bogdanov and during the meeting Bogdanov signed two protocols -- one for the holding company and one for AO Surgutneftegaz -- about the elimination of violations of Russian law arising from the issue of ordinary shares," the commission spokesman said.
Surgut Holding acquired an entire new issue of 500 million ordinary shares and 34.02 million preferred shares in AO Surgutneftegaz in October, raising its stake to 43.5 percent from 38 percent.
The shares were bought for prices below the market price.

The federal commission spokesman also said that Surgut Holding and ZAO Surgutskiye Investitstii (Surgut Investments) would agree to pay an additional 200 billion roubles for the ordinary shares by April 1 and that this would bring the share price close to the market level.
Industry sources said Surgut Investments was a vehicle for Surgut Holding which had bought up the bulk of the share issue.
"The federal commission considers that these measures will ensure shareholders' rights are protected," the spokesman said.
Surgut Holding said in October the issue was made in accordance with the company's charter, approved by shareholders in June and that it was intended to strengthen control over the subsidiary.
Surgutneftegaz shares fell sharply immediately after the issue but have recovered some ground since.

Shares rose on Tuesday on news of the agreement with the commission. The ordinary shares stood on Tuesday at 0910 GMT at $0.420, after closing on Monday at $0.405. The preferred shares were at $0.297, after $0.276.
